notes.title: DEV BLOG #10 - Demo update - Patch notes
notes.notes:
I've updated the demo with the following changes:

[i]Bugfixes:

- Victory/Defeat jingles played at wrong volume
- Loading a map with preplaced warriors could cause loading to end premature
- When placing torches radius could show unvalid locations (unreachable corners)
- Not able to cancel building some objects
- Missing bounce effect when building weapon racks
- Various text fixes (misaligments, typos)
- Removed leftover debug code


Added features:

- Reworked gold storage. No more individiual storage, chests now contribute to a pool
- Goblins carrying gold will recalculate paths if a new chest becomes available
- Reworked Destroy/sell. The player will now recieve half golds worth of objects deleted
  with the destroy tool. Refunds are instant any excess gold will be dumped outside shrine
- Deleting (canceling) unbuilt object now gives back all gold
- Added number effect when selling
- Rewrote tutorial texts to reflect the reworks above
- Newly available food will prioritize angry goblins
- Newly available beds will prioritize angry goblins
- Idle goblins will prioritize building over gathering and digging
- Wall rendering optimizations
- Added more map decorations (doodads)
- Slighty increased decay time for dirt debris
- Added more goblin names
- Map format now stores music track

Balance:

- Tresurey floor lowered to 50 gold (100)
- Torches lowered to 50 gold (100)
- Research time reduced to 120s (180s)
- Goblin starting hunger value raised to 70-90 (30-80)
- Minor tweaks to the tutorial maps

(previous values in parenteses)
[/i]

As you can see I've been pretty busy. The demo will probably be updated once I get translations in place, but going forward I will be focusing on the full game.
As always, thank you for your support!

notes.title: DEV BLOG #6 - Graphical update
notes.notes:
Goblin Colony is a 2D game with hand-drawn pixel graphics viewed from a top-down perspective (or a mixed top-down oblique perspective, I guess, if you want to get real technical).

As everything on the screen is a flat image (sprites), there really is no concept of mass like there would be in a 3D environment. This makes it tricky to convey a sense of depth, and things can look a bit flat (because they are).

While I’m using shades and baked-in transparency shadows for most sprites, I always wanted the environment to have a bit more depth but couldn’t find a good way of doing it without sacrificing performance. Until now.

Now all walls cast shadows, and objects get an added effect similar to ambient occlusion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43479287/769b89ab809655502011874d00a48fbe6297c0c4.gif[/img]
[i]before/after[/i]

The effect isn’t final as I’m still fine-tuning the intensity, but I’m very happy with this change. I think it’s a dramatic improvement that sets the mood for exploring dank caves. Hope you like it :)

As always, thank you for your support! Until next time.
